# R13 · Your vehicle: maintenance, insurance, towing, fuel & off-road: questions

**Rules half** · 13 questions · [Study guide](../guide/R13-vehicle-insurance-towing.md) · [All rules topics](../README.md)

### 1. Replace your tires when the tread is less than how deep?

*Exact numbers*

- **A.** 0.5 millimetres
- **B.** 1.5 millimetres
- **C.** 5 millimetres
- **D.** 3 millimetres

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**B. 1.5 millimetres**

Or when the tread-wear indicators touch the road.

> 📖 Handbook: "Replace tires when the tread is less than 1.5 millimetres deep or when tread-wear indicators touch the road."

</details>

---

### 2. You sell your car. What happens to the licence plates?

*Word traps*

- **A.** You keep them: plates belong to the owner, not the car
- **B.** You must destroy them
- **C.** They stay on the car for the new owner
- **D.** You mail them to the buyer

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**A. You keep them: plates belong to the owner, not the car**

Ontario uses a plate-to-owner system. Remove your plates when you sell.

> 📖 Handbook: "This means that vehicle licence plates move with the vehicle owner, not the vehicle. When you sell or change vehicles, you must remove your plates."

</details>

---

### 3. May passengers ride in a house trailer while it's being towed?

*Word traps*

- **A.** Yes, on short trips
- **B.** Yes, in a boat trailer only
- **C.** Yes, if they wear seatbelts
- **D.** No: you may not carry anyone in any trailer being towed

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**D. No: you may not carry anyone in any trailer being towed**

No passengers in any trailer, including house and boat trailers.

> 📖 Handbook: "You may not carry any person in any trailer, including a house or boat trailer, when it is being towed."

</details>

---

### 4. How many trailers may you tow behind a regular (non-commercial) vehicle?

*Word traps*

- **A.** As many as the hitch can hold
- **B.** Only one
- **C.** Two, if they're small
- **D.** Three

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**B. Only one**

It is against the law to tow more than one trailer behind a non-commercial vehicle.

> 📖 Handbook: "It is against the law to tow more than one trailer behind non-commercial vehicles."

</details>

---

### 5. You're towing a trailer and a big truck passes you. The wind makes your trailer sway. What should you do?

*Best action*

- **A.** Pull onto the shoulder at full speed
- **B.** Brake hard right away
- **C.** Steer sharply the other way
- **D.** Don't brake: steer carefully back into position (a slight increase in speed may help)

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**D. Don't brake: steer carefully back into position (a slight increase in speed may help)**

Braking can make the sway worse.

> 📖 Handbook: "When you experience this, do not brake. Carefully steer your vehicle and trailer back into position. A slight increase in speed may help."

</details>

---

### 6. You're backing up with a trailer and want the trailer to go to the RIGHT. Which way do you steer?

*Best action*

- **A.** It depends on the trailer's weight
- **B.** Keep the wheel straight
- **C.** To the right
- **D.** To the left

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**D. To the left**

Backing a trailer is opposite: steer left to back right.

> 📖 Handbook: "To back up to the right, steer to the left."

</details>

---

### 7. You'll be parked for a few minutes. To save fuel and cut pollution, what should you do?

*Best action*

- **A.** Leave it running so it stays warm
- **B.** Turn it off only if parked over 10 minutes
- **C.** Turn off the engine if you'll be parked for more than 10 seconds
- **D.** Rev the engine every minute

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**C. Turn off the engine if you'll be parked for more than 10 seconds**

Even in cold weather, engines warm up within 30 seconds.

> 📖 Handbook: "Turn off your vehicle if parked more than 10 seconds."

</details>

---

### 8. Which of these helps your car use less fuel?

*Best action*

- **A.** Idling to warm up for 10 minutes
- **B.** Leaving the roof rack on all year
- **C.** Topping off the gas tank every time
- **D.** Keeping your tires properly inflated

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**D. Keeping your tires properly inflated**

Proper tire pressure saves fuel and reduces tire wear and emissions.

> 📖 Handbook: "Keep your tires properly inflated to reduce your fuel bill, emissions and tire wear."

</details>

### 9. Is car insurance required in Ontario?

*Laws & consequences*

- **A.** Only if you have a loan on the car
- **B.** Yes: every vehicle registered in Ontario must be insured
- **C.** Only on highways
- **D.** Only for new drivers

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**B. Yes: every vehicle registered in Ontario must be insured**

You must show proof of insurance to register a vehicle or renew its registration.

> 📖 Handbook: "Ontario has compulsory automobile insurance. This means every vehicle registered in the province must be insured."

</details>

---

### 10. Who can inspect your vehicle and take it off the road if it's unsafe?

*Laws & consequences*

- **A.** Only after a collision
- **B.** Only your mechanic
- **C.** A police officer or Ministry of Transportation inspector, at any time
- **D.** No one, if your registration is valid

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**C. A police officer or Ministry of Transportation inspector, at any time**

It's illegal to drive a vehicle in dangerous condition.

> 📖 Handbook: "A police officer or Ministry of Transportation inspector can examine your vehicle, its equipment and any trailer attached to it, at any time."

</details>

### 11. What is the heaviest trailer you may tow with a G1, G2 or G licence?

*Laws & consequences*

- **A.** 4,600 kg (gross vehicle weight)
- **B.** There's no limit
- **C.** 11,000 kg
- **D.** 1,360 kg

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**A. 4,600 kg (gross vehicle weight)**

Heavier trailers may need a higher licence class or a permit. (1,360 kg is when the trailer needs its own brakes.)

> 📖 Handbook: "You must have a valid driver's licence (Class G1, G2 or G) or higher class of licence to tow a trailer with a gross vehicle weight of up to 4,600 kilograms."

</details>

---

### 12. A trailer (with its load) weighs 1,360 kg or more. What must it have?

*Laws & consequences*

- **A.** An orange slow-moving sign
- **B.** A licence plate on the front
- **C.** Brakes strong enough to stop and hold it
- **D.** A second hitch ball

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**C. Brakes strong enough to stop and hold it**

1,360 kg = brakes required.

> 📖 Handbook: "If your trailer has a gross trailer weight, vehicle and load of 1,360 kilograms or more, it must have brakes strong enough to stop and hold the trailer."

</details>

---

### 13. How must safety chains be attached between a car and trailer?

*Laws & consequences*

- **A.** Crossed under the trailer tongue
- **B.** Safety chains aren't needed
- **C.** Straight, not crossed
- **D.** Wrapped around the bumper

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**A. Crossed under the trailer tongue**

Crossed chains stop the tongue from dropping onto the road if the hitch comes loose.

> 📖 Handbook: "If safety chains are used, they must be crossed under the tongue to prevent the tongue from drop­ping to the road if the primary hitch accidentally disconnects."

</details>
